security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by SimPy terms such as env, request, timeout, and Markdown code fences. The only confirmed issue is local CSV export to caller-provided filenames, which is legitimate but should be constrained to avoid unsafe overwrites.

remediation.issue: CSV export accepts arbitrary output filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Validate export paths, avoid overwriting existing files by default, and document that exports write to the local filesystem.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples show unrestricted CSV file writes.
remediation.suggestion: Use examples that write to a clearly user-selected output directory and mention overwrite behavior.

content.value_statement: Modeling queues, capacity, and resource contention can be hard to structure correctly. This skill gives Codex and Claude focused SimPy patterns for building, monitoring, and analyzing simulations.
actual_capabilities: Explains SimPy environments, processes, events, resources, containers, and stores.
Provides queue and resource contention templates for Python simulations.
Shows monitoring patterns for wait times, utilization, queue length, and throughput.
Includes reusable scripts for a basic simulation and resource monitoring.
Documents process interaction patterns such as signaling, interrupts, and parallel workflows.
Covers real-time simulation concepts for wall-clock synchronized runs.
limitations: It does not replace statistical validation or domain-specific model review.
It focuses on SimPy, not continuous differential-equation simulation.
CSV export examples can write local files when called by the user.
It does not provide a graphical simulation interface.

use_cases.title: Plan Service Capacity
use_cases.description: Model arrival rates, service times, and staff capacity to estimate wait times and throughput.

use_cases.title: Test Manufacturing Flow
use_cases.description: Simulate machines, buffers, interruptions, and bottlenecks before changing a production process.

use_cases.title: Teach Event Simulation
use_cases.description: Create small SimPy examples that demonstrate events, resources, stores, and process coordination.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a simple SimPy queue simulation with one server, random arrivals, service times, and a short results summary.

prompt_templates.title: Add Resource Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my SimPy model to track queue length, utilization, wait time, and throughput. Explain each metric clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Capacity Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SimPy experiment that compares two, three, and four resources under the same arrivals and reports the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Model Interruptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SimPy model with preemptive resources, interruptions, recovery time, and monitoring for lost capacity.

output_examples.input: A call center receives customers every two minutes and has three agents.
output_examples.output: A SimPy model with customer arrivals, agent resources, wait-time tracking, utilization reporting, and guidance for changing capacity.

output_examples.input: A factory line has one bottleneck machine and variable repair delays.
output_examples.output: A simulation design with machine processes, repair interruptions, buffer behavior, and metrics for throughput and downtime.

output_examples.input: A warehouse needs a reusable monitor for several loading docks.
output_examples.output: A monitoring approach that records resource requests, queue lengths, utilization, and a concise operational report.

best_practices: Define entities, resources, process steps, and metrics before writing the model.
Set random seeds and run repeated experiments when comparing scenarios.
Validate simple cases against expected results before trusting complex simulations.
anti_patterns: Do not use blocking Python calls inside SimPy processes.
Do not compare capacity options without using the same arrival assumptions.
Do not treat one random simulation run as a final forecast.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps build Python SimPy models for queues, resources, events, and monitored process flows.

faq.question: Does it run simulations automatically?
faq.answer: It provides templates and helper scripts. The user chooses when to run generated Python code.

faq.question: Can it model continuous systems?
faq.answer: It is best for discrete events. Continuous models usually need SciPy or another numerical tool.

faq.question: Does it support resource monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for utilization, queue length, wait time, and CSV export.

faq.question: Is network access required?
faq.answer: No. The detected request examples are SimPy resource requests, not HTTP requests.

faq.question: What should users validate?
faq.answer: Users should validate assumptions, distributions, warm-up periods, and sample sizes for each simulation study.
